Carson Gross argues that Markdown is evolving from documentation into a form of source code within agentic coding workflows. He proposes that developers should check Markdown files—describing architectural and implementation intent—into a `/src/md` directory alongside the generated code. This practice aims to capture the "intent" that is currently lost during ephemeral LLM prompting sessions.

In this workflow, Markdown serves as a specification, while the generated code and tests function as the implementation and automated verification of that specification.

entry.title: The Evolution of Graphical User Interface Design
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | youtube.com | discussion

Mid-century innovations such as the trackball and Ivan Sutherland's Sketchpad laid the groundwork for the Graphical User Interface (GUI). Douglas Engelbart’s 1968 "Mother of All Demos" significantly advanced the field by demonstrating the mouse, hyperlinks, and word processing, while subsequent work at Xerox PARC through Smalltalk and the desktop metaphor established the framework for modern computing.

The implementation of the "WIMP" (Windows, Icons, Menu, Pointer) model replaced text-based command interfaces with a skeuomorphic representation of a physical workspace. While research at MIT and Xerox PARC provided the fundamental technology, the commercialization of these ideas by companies like Apple moved the interface into the consumer mainstream. This shift transitioned computers from specialized mathematical tools into intuitive, personal devices.

entry.title: Fast Hash Functions Exhibit Significant Collision Weaknesses Under AI Analysis
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | thomasahle.com | discussion | hacker news

Many popular non-cryptographic hash functions, including xxHash and MurmurHash, are susceptible to adversarial inputs that trigger high collision rates. Using AI-driven analysis, researchers found that many of these hashes perform significantly worse—sometimes by as much as 20 bits—than their expected collision bounds when encountering specific data patterns.

The findings indicate that provably secure hashes, such as ChainHash, can match the performance of heuristic-based alternatives on modern hardware. This suggests that the traditional trade-off between execution speed and provable collision resistance may be unnecessary, particularly as AI makes it easier to exploit vulnerabilities in previously obscure implementations.
